subject.title: config: use datetime suffix for config backup files instead of numeric rotation

question: Should timestamped config backups preserve or convert existing numbered `.bak.N` recovery points before switching formats, or may first-run cleanup delete them?
rationale: Config backups may be a user's only recovery copy, and the repository treats config migration and persisted recovery behavior as compatibility-sensitive rather than an automation-only choice.

options.title: Preserve Legacy Recovery Points
options.body: Require this PR or a replacement to retain or convert `.bak.1`..`.bak.4` into the new bounded timestamp retention set before deleting them.

options.title: Accept Timestamp-Only Reset
options.body: Allow first-run cleanup to prune numbered backups, but document the upgrade behavior and require explicit maintainer acceptance of the recovery-point loss.

options.title: Keep Numeric Ring For Now
options.body: Reject the naming change until maintainers choose a broader config-backup layout and recovery contract.

recommendation.title: Preserve Legacy Recovery Points
recommendation.body: Require this PR or a replacement to retain or convert `.bak.1`..`.bak.4` into the new bounded timestamp retention set before deleting them.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest visible history and review context around config backup recovery semantics.
